title: RBI Repo Rate Hike: Impact on Your Home Loan EMI
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has increased the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) to 5.50% on October 7, 2026. This hike will directly affect your home loa.

faq.a: The repo rate is the interest rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) by selling government securities with an agreement to repurchase them later. It's a key monetary policy tool.

faq.q: How often does the RBI change the repo rate?
faq.a: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meets at least six times a year, typically every two months, to review the economic situation and decide on policy rates, including the repo rate. Changes can also happen off-cycle if deemed necessary.

faq.q: Does a repo rate hike affect fixed-rate home loans?
faq.a: No, a repo rate hike does not directly affect fixed-rate home loans. The interest rate on fixed-rate loans remains constant throughout the loan tenure, irrespective of changes in the repo rate or other market benchmarks.

faq.q: Can I switch my home loan to another bank after a repo rate hike?
faq.a: Yes, you can consider a home loan balance transfer to another bank offering a lower interest rate, especially if your current bank's rates have become uncompetitive after the hike. This can help reduce your EMI or shorten your tenure.

faq.q: How does this hike impact new home loan applicants?
faq.a: New home loan applicants will face higher interest rates compared to before the hike. Banks will price their new loans based on the revised repo rate, leading to higher EMIs for the same loan amount and tenure.

faq.q: Is there any tax benefit related to home loan interest?
faq.a: Yes, under Section 24(b) of the Income Tax Act, you can claim a deduction of up to ₹2 lakhs on the interest paid on a home loan for a self-occupied property. For rented properties, the entire interest paid can be deducted.
A basis point is a common unit of measure in finance, equal to one-hundredth of a percentage point. So, 25 bps equals 0.25%.
